charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt & Interest Coverage

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash, debt and interest coverage
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted), with interest coverage (EBITDA / interest expense, from the trust's MAS Appendix 6 disclosure) on the right axis.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: coverage has fallen from 5.6x in FY2018 to 2.9x in FY2025 and FY2026 as the debt book repriced at higher rates — the headroom side of the same leverage story as Gearing.

What to watch:

  • Coverage below ~3x leaves little room before a rate shock pressures distributions
  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

dpu.title: Distribution per unit (DPU)
dpu.content:
DPU is the cash distribution paid per unit for the period — the headline return metric for a REIT, distinct from EPS because it is paid from distributable income rather than accounting net income.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: DPU grew every year from 7.35 cents (FY2014) to a peak of 9.011 cents (FY2023), then fell for three straight years to 7.262 cents (FY2026) as higher-for-longer interest expense, enlarged unit count and China/South Korea portfolio weakness outpaced net property income growth.

What to watch:

  • Whether DPU has stabilised or is still declining
  • Distributable income coverage versus units issued (dilution from equity fund-raising)
  • Compare against the Interest Coverage chart — both turned down together

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Mapletree Logistics Trust: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
